id: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Unintentional Transgressions 2:1
q_practical: If I start doing something by accident but finish it on purpose, do I still owe a penalty offering?
q_conceptual: Why does an act have to be a mistake from start to finish to count as accidental?

id: Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 1:15
q_practical: How much of my field's harvest am I required to leave for poor people to gather?
q_conceptual: Why does the required share for the poor change with the size of the field and how many poor people there are?

q_practical: Can spices like ginger and pepper become ritually unclean the way other foods can?
q_conceptual: Why does something you eat only for flavor, not for its own sake, escape the rules of ritual impurity?

id: Mishneh Torah, Other Sources of Defilement 2:9
q_practical: If an animal has trouble giving birth and a limb of the unborn calf falls off, is that limb treated as meat from a dead animal?
q_conceptual: Why does the order of events during a difficult birth change how the meat is classified?

q_practical: Should I hold it in or go to the bathroom right away when I need to?
q_conceptual: Why is keeping the body healthy treated as a spiritual obligation and not just a practical one?

q_practical: I made a vow conditional on a pile of grain reaching a certain amount, but some of it turned out to be stolen — does my vow still count?
q_conceptual: Why do doubtful vows get resolved leniently rather than strictly?

id: Mishneh Torah, Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee 8:14
q_practical: Can I buy raw flax from a farmer I suspect of illegally selling produce grown in the fallow year?
q_conceptual: Why does processing a raw material change whether it's still treated as fallow-year produce?

q_practical: My neighbor wants to build a wall facing mine and close off the gap between them — can I stop him?
q_conceptual: Why does leaving a gap between two facing walls matter for the ground underneath them?

id: Mishneh Torah, Robbery and Lost Property 6:13
q_practical: If I knock forgotten olives down from a tree, can someone else just take them from where they fell?
q_conceptual: At what point does an ownerless item actually become someone's property?

q_practical: Does a child automatically inherit from a parent who isn't Jewish?
q_conceptual: Why does inheritance law defer to local custom in some cases but not others?

q_practical: Is there a minimum amount of grain I have to set aside as a priestly gift?
q_conceptual: Why would a single kernel technically satisfy an obligation that applies to an entire harvest?

q_practical: What kinds of household items can become ritually unclean?
q_conceptual: Why are only certain materials — cloth, leather, wood, metal, bone, and clay — treated as capable of carrying impurity?

id: Mishneh Torah, Robbery and Lost Property 13:17
q_practical: If I find lost property, sell it, and the money then gets stolen from me, am I still responsible for repaying the owner?
q_conceptual: Why does having permission to use someone else's money make you liable even for losses you couldn't control?

q_practical: Can a witness who signed a contract later claim they signed it under duress?
q_conceptual: Why does it matter whether a document's validity depends entirely on the witnesses' word?

q_practical: If I plan to spend the night at a certain spot for the Sabbath but end up turning back before I get there, does the plan still count?
q_conceptual: Why does merely intending and setting out toward a place count as if you'd actually arrived there?

q_practical: I hurt someone's feelings — is just apologizing to God enough to be forgiven?
q_conceptual: Why can't repentance alone fix a wrong done to another person?

q_practical: Someone stole my field and later got me to say in front of witnesses that I'd sold it to him — does that count as a real sale?
q_conceptual: Why doesn't a coerced acknowledgment of a sale count as proof of ownership?

id: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Unintentional Transgressions 15:7
q_practical: If a former high priest makes an honest mistake after losing his position, does he bring the same offering as an active high priest?
q_conceptual: Why do some special privileges of the office end when someone is removed from it, while others don't?

id: Mishneh Torah, One Who Injures a Person or Property 2:3
q_practical: If I burn someone in a spot that doesn't leave a real wound, what do I owe them?
q_conceptual: Why does the type of harm determine which categories of compensation apply?

q_practical: If I vow to abstain from wine for just one hour, how long am I actually bound by it?
q_conceptual: Why can't a vow of this kind be measured in hours?

id: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 2:15
q_practical: When during the year do I switch from mentioning dew to mentioning rain in my prayers?
q_conceptual: Why does the wording of a prayer change with the seasons?

id: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 6:19
q_practical: I donated money for a purpose by mistake — can I get it back?
q_conceptual: Why does a donation made in error not count as final?

id: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 1:3
q_practical: Can someone give an official religious ruling after having a few drinks?
q_conceptual: Why does being even slightly impaired disqualify someone from making a legal decision?

id: Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 11:10
q_practical: Do temporary shelters like tents or a bathhouse count as houses when it comes to impurity from foreign dwellings?
q_conceptual: Why does a structure need to be a permanent dwelling for this impurity rule to apply?

q_practical: If I pick olives to sell at the market, do they become susceptible to spoiling ritually just from being picked?
q_conceptual: Why does a food only become vulnerable to impurity once it's been wetted the way its owner intended?

q_practical: Can I pay the person watching my crops with the priestly gift I owe instead of their wages?
q_conceptual: Why is it considered disrespectful to hand over a sacred gift as if it were ordinary payment?

id: Mishneh Torah, Service on the Day of Atonement 1:2
q_practical: Can any priest perform the special Yom Kippur sacrifices, or does it have to be the head priest?
q_conceptual: Why does the text specifically require the high priest to be married to perform these rites?

q_practical: If someone steals my sheep and sells it before I give up hope of getting it back, do I still own the sheep?
q_conceptual: Why does the owner's state of mind affect whether a stolen item's sale is valid?

id: Mishneh Torah, Vessels of the Sanctuary and Those Who Serve Therein 9:4
q_practical: How many bells and pomegranates were attached to the hem of the priestly robe?
q_conceptual: Why did the decorative pattern need to alternate bells and pomegranates rather than group them separately?

q_practical: Two people's animals were with a shepherd, one died, and now no one can tell whose surviving animal is the firstborn — what happens to it?
q_conceptual: How is ownership split when there's no way to identify which animal belongs to whom?

q_practical: If my ox injures a person, how much do I have to pay compared to if I injured them myself?
q_conceptual: Why is an owner's liability for their animal's actions treated as property damage rather than personal injury?

id: Mishneh Torah, First Fruits and other Gifts to Priests Outside the Sanctuary 9:17
q_practical: Can I split a single cut of meat between two different priests when giving the required gifts?
q_conceptual: Why does a gift have to be a meaningful portion rather than just any share, however small?

q_practical: Does it matter what order I give away my various crop gifts and tithes?
q_conceptual: Why is there a required sequence for giving away different portions of a harvest, even though doing it out of order still works?

id: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Those with Incomplete Atonement 2:5
q_practical: Can an unusual discharge in a nursing baby be blamed on the mother's health instead of the baby's?
q_conceptual: Why does the cause of a bodily symptom, not just the symptom itself, determine its legal status?

q_practical: If one of my cows kicks another cow that's lying down, am I liable for the full damage or only part?
q_conceptual: Why is an animal's owner held to a lower standard for unusual behavior than for typical behavior?

q_practical: What happens to a king's horse and carriage after he dies?
q_conceptual: Why would harming an animal be part of honoring a ruler's death?

id: Mishneh Torah, Other Sources of Defilement 1:12
q_practical: If two small scraps of meat are stuck together on a skewer, does touching them make me impure?
q_conceptual: Why does something joined by a person, rather than naturally, not count as a single unit for one kind of impurity but does for another?

q_practical: I bought something from one of five people, lied under oath about it, and now all five claim I owe them — do I have to pay everyone?
q_conceptual: Why would someone be required to pay multiple people when only one of them could actually be telling the truth?

id: Mishneh Torah, Woman Suspected of Infidelity 4:10
q_practical: If part of the writing on a ritual scroll doesn't fully erase, is the ritual still valid?
q_conceptual: Why does the entire text need to be written in one continuous sitting rather than letter by letter with erasures in between?

q_practical: If someone's purification is due on the Sabbath, does that delay them from bringing the Passover sacrifice?
q_conceptual: Why can a lesser prohibition override a rule tied to a much more serious sacrifice?

q_practical: If a clay pot breaks, is the broken piece still capable of becoming ritually unclean?
q_conceptual: Why are broken pieces of clay containers treated differently from broken pieces of anything else?

q_practical: If prayers for rain go unanswered, should I still throw a wedding or start a big renovation?
q_conceptual: Why would a community deliberately scale back joyful activities during a drought?

q_practical: My grandfather had two sons who both died before him — how is his estate split between their children?
q_conceptual: Why does being descended from the firstborn son affect how much a grandchild inherits?

q_practical: My animal wandered into my neighbor's garden once, I got it back, and it went back on its own — am I liable?
q_conceptual: Why does an animal returning to a place on its own count as the owner's fault?

q_practical: Can a husband write his own divorce document instead of having a scribe do it?
q_conceptual: Why does who physically writes a legal document affect whether it's valid?

q_practical: Two people share a well, and neither of us covered it — which one of us is liable if an animal falls in?
q_conceptual: Why does responsibility shift from one partner to the other over time instead of staying shared?

q_practical: Why is it considered so important to give a proper eulogy for a respected person?
q_conceptual: What does the way we treat a death say about the value placed on the person's life?

id: Mishneh Torah, Things Forbidden on the Altar 3:8
q_practical: Can a newborn animal be offered as a sacrifice right away?
q_conceptual: Why does a sacrifice offered too early count as invalid but not carry the usual punishment?

q_practical: How much water and how far up my hands do I need to wash before eating bread?
q_conceptual: Why do the same rules for what disqualifies a ritual bath also apply to washing hands?

q_practical: Can a saddle blanket or riding cushion become ritually unclean?
q_conceptual: Why does an object become susceptible to impurity specifically because a person sits on it?

id: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 4:2
q_practical: I'm on a trip and it's time to pray but I have no water nearby — what do I do?
q_conceptual: Why does the required distance to water determine whether you can substitute something else for washing?

q_practical: If a priest and someone who's taken a special vow both come across an abandoned corpse that needs burying, who has to do it?
q_conceptual: Why does a temporary vow yield to an obligation that a permanent status doesn't?

q_practical: Is there a blessing to say before and after going to a public bathhouse?
q_conceptual: Why would visiting a bathhouse be treated as dangerous enough to warrant a prayer for safety?

q_practical: If I buy a nursing animal from someone who isn't Jewish, do I need to worry the milk belongs to a different animal's firstborn?
q_conceptual: Why is it assumed that an animal producing milk has already given birth before?

q_practical: Do the rules about liability for damage caused by animals apply outside the land of Israel too?
q_conceptual: Why would a law be specified as applying everywhere rather than only in one place?

id: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 4:13
q_practical: Why do the priestly work groups sometimes get fewer loaves of bread in a given week?
q_conceptual: Why does having only one day free from duty affect how much bread a group receives?

id: Mishneh Torah, Murderer and the Preservation of Life 5:7
q_practical: After someone flees to a city of refuge, who decides whether they're eventually released or executed?
q_conceptual: Why does the case get sent back to the court where the killing happened rather than being decided in the refuge city?

q_practical: If I swear off eating dates but then eat non-kosher meat, have I broken a false oath?
q_conceptual: Why does including a forbidden item in an oath about permitted items still make the oath take effect?

q_practical: My father paid for my wedding and gave me a gift, then passed away — do I have to repay that gift out of my own share?
q_conceptual: Why does who paid for the wedding determine whether a gift is repaid from the whole estate or from one person's share?

id: Mishneh Torah, Robbery and Lost Property 11:13
q_practical: I found a large sack in a field, but carrying it isn't something someone of my standing would normally do — am I still obligated to return it?
q_conceptual: Why does personal dignity affect whether you're required to return a lost item?

q_practical: If good deeds are really rewarded in the afterlife, why does the Torah talk about earthly rewards like prosperity and peace?
q_conceptual: How can promises of material blessing and hardship be reconciled with a reward that's ultimately spiritual?

q_practical: If I accidentally eat a priestly gift I wasn't allowed to touch, what do I owe?
q_conceptual: Why is there a minimum amount you must eat before you're liable to repay it with a penalty?

q_practical: When do I become obligated to tithe vegetables I'm selling — when I bundle them or when I fill the crate?
q_conceptual: Why does the packaging method determine the exact point produce becomes liable for tithes?

id: Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 8:6
q_practical: Can a synagogue sell a candelabra someone donated in memory of themselves?
q_conceptual: Why does whether a donor's name is still attached to an item affect if it can be resold?

q_practical: If an animal swallowed something that could puncture its intestines, is its meat still kosher?
q_conceptual: Why does one intestine being coiled around another change whether a puncture makes the meat forbidden?

id: Mishneh Torah, Leavened and Unleavened Bread 6:1
q_practical: Do I have to eat matzah on every night of Passover, or just the first one?
q_conceptual: Why is eating matzah an obligation in its own right rather than something tied to a sacrifice?

id: Mishneh Torah, The Sanhedrin and the Penalties within Their Jurisdiction 23:4
q_practical: Can a judge hear a case involving someone who recently lent them something?
q_conceptual: Why does the ability to reciprocate a loan change whether a judge is considered impartial?

q_practical: Do I have to say a blessing out loud for it to count?
q_conceptual: Why would a blessing recited silently still fulfill the obligation?

q_practical: I only found out days later that a close relative died — do I still observe the full mourning period?
q_conceptual: Why does finding mourners still gathered change how the mourning period is counted?

q_practical: Are first fruits considered the same category of gift as other crop offerings to priests?
q_conceptual: Why does a term only explicitly used for some offerings get extended to cover one that isn't named directly?

q_practical: If it doesn't rain on time in a place outside Israel, when do individuals start fasting for rain?
q_conceptual: Why does the fasting schedule for rain depend on the local climate rather than being fixed everywhere?

q_practical: If I lied about what happened to a borrowed ox that actually died, am I still liable even though the lie didn't get me out of paying?

q_practical: I paid for produce as a minor heir but didn't physically take possession yet, and the price dropped — can I back out of the deal?
q_conceptual: Why does actually taking possession, not just paying, determine when a sale is final?

q_practical: Does an examiner have to check hidden areas of the body like the armpits for skin conditions?
q_conceptual: Why does the visibility of a spot to the naked eye determine whether it counts under this law?

id: Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 1:9

q_practical: Do the white strings and the blue string on ritual fringes count as two separate requirements?
q_conceptual: Why are two different colored threads treated as parts of one single commandment rather than two?

id: Mishneh Torah, Sanctification of the New Month 18:9

q_conceptual: Why does the calendar calculation aim only to make a sighting possible, not guarantee it?

q_practical: Is it against the rules for two men to be alone together in private?
q_conceptual: Why would avoiding a situation that isn't technically forbidden still be considered admirable?

q_practical: What happens to a person's consciousness after death?
q_conceptual: Why is the ultimate reward described as something the soul can experience without needing a body?

id: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 2:4
q_practical: What's the penalty for a priest who wanders into a sacred inner room he's not authorized to enter?
q_conceptual: Why does the punishment for entering the innermost sacred space differ from entering the area just outside it?
